data.narrative:
Cellcolabs is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Mattias Bernow that has raised $37M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a private peer universe of 8 companies in Biotech & Health, alongside 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L).

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method uses the company's $37M total raised as a baseline valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A-to-next-stage progression, yielding $74M. The peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage peer data; while 8 same-sector companies exist, none met the threshold of three or more direct comparables at matching stage and valuation tier. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (median 5.5x across the three public tickers) cannot be applied absent revenue disclosure, standard for private companies.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $63M to $85M, with a median of $74M. Given the single-method foundation, material uncertainty remains around stage-appropriate multiples and peer validation. Revenue generation and clinical/technical milestones will be critical to narrowing this band in future rounds. The analysis is constrained by limited comparable depth at the Series A stage within this sector.
